title: Determining the value of manual therapy at different starting points during a medical strengthening intervention in patients with chronic specific low back pain related to perceived pain, quality of life and morphology and functionality of their paraspinal lumbar extensor muscles - a randomised controlled study
summary:
Atrophy and fatty infiltration in the parspinal back muscles are known to be invoved in the development of chronic low back pain. Interventions that focus on specific conditioning of these muscles have shown good clinical outcomes. As chronic low back is also influenced by other (psycho-social) factors it is recommended to apply a holistic approach and to combine different treatment approaches in order to achieve the best possible results.
Therefore the aim of this study is to explore the effects of combining specific exercise with manual therapy. Especially the additive value of manual therapy and the optimal timing of this intervention will be studied. Patients suffering from pain in the lumbar spine region for more than 3 months and a diagnosed disorder in that region (primarily disk herniations) are included.
All patients go through an exercise intervention including specific conditioning of the paraspinal back muscles for in total 18 sessions (2x/week). One group (1) receives 4 sessions of manual therapy prior to the start of the exercise intervention. Patients in group 2 receive manual therapy in a later phase (from session 9 onwards) parallel to the exercise intervention. Patients in group 3 receive no additional manual therapy.
The specific aim is to study if early appliance of manual therapy leads to faster and better results. Furthermore, the value of manual therapy in general is analyzed. In each session the current pain levels (0-10) are taken. Furthermore, at three time points (before session 1, after 4 sessions, after 18 exercise sessions) several other parameters are taken. That includes thickness of the muscle and fascia (via ultrasound), muscle activity (via EMG), subjective statement on life quality (SF-36) and lumbar spine function (ODI questionnaire). At those three time points mean values will be compared between the groups.

interventions.name: Group 1: early manual therapy before start of the training
Group 2: manual therapy later on (from session 9 (out of 18 sessions)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- chronic low back pain (at least 3 months)
- written consent
Exclusion criteria:
- back surgery in the patient‘s history
- low back pain that is rated < 3 on the NRS scale 0-10
- regular use of pain killers at the beginning of the intervention
- any additional therapy or treatment that is planned during the intervention
